title: Statistics - Lesson 8: Percentile Rank Practice
description: Practice calculating and interpreting percentile rank using ordered data.

questions.question: Using the below-score convention, what does percentile rank measure?
options: The percent of values below a given score
The percent correct on a test
The difference between the highest and lowest scores
questions.explanation: Percentile rank describes relative standing by finding the percent of data values below the given score.

questions.question: In the ordered data set 42, 48, 53, 59, 64, 70, how many values are below 64? Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: The values below 64 are 42, 48, 53, and 59, so there are 4 values below the score.

questions.question: In the ordered data set 10, 12, 15, 18, 20, what is the percentile rank of 18 using the below-score convention?
questions.explanation: Three of the five values are below 18, so (3/5) x 100 = 60.

questions.question: A score at the 75th percentile is higher than about 75% of the values in the data set.
questions.explanation: A percentile rank compares one value with the rest of the data set; the 75th percentile means about 75% of values are below it.

questions.question: A data set has 20 values. A score has 14 values below it. What is its percentile rank using the below-score convention?
questions.explanation: Use (14/20) x 100 = 70, so the score is at the 70th percentile.

questions.question: Which situation would make the at-or-below convention give a different answer from the below-score convention?
options: The target score appears in the data set
The data are written in increasing order
The data set has an even number of values
The scores are all whole numbers
questions.explanation: At-or-below counts the target score itself, while below-score does not. That difference matters when the target score is included in the data set.

questions.question: A score has 9 values below it out of 12 total values. What is the percentile rank? Enter the percent without the percent sign.
questions.explanation: (9/12) x 100 = 75, so the score is at the 75th percentile.

questions.question: In one sentence, interpret this result: A score of 88 is at the 80th percentile in a class quiz data set.
questions.correctAnswer: A score of 88 is higher than about 80% of the class quiz scores.
questions.explanation: A good interpretation names the score, the percentile rank, and the group being compared.
